llm.summary: This fact-checking skill warrants review because it gives conflicting API-key privacy instructions and insufficiently limits its automatically updated runner.

dimensions.detail: The documented dependencies and optional conversion packages are proportionate. However, the [current upstream client](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sensedeal/cue-skills/main/cue-research/scripts/cue_api.py) recommends --sandbox danger-full-access for network failures, unnecessarily broadening access beyond network connectivity.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Lines 101–106 clone or update an unpinned external repository, and line 120 executes its Python runner. No review checkpoint or restricted execution boundary is specified before changed code gains access to the configured credential.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md lines 113 and 165 prohibit the agent from viewing the API key, while line 184 asks users to send it to the agent. This creates a concrete conflict about credential privacy; programmatic authentication alone is expected.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The runner checkout, configuration, reports, and resumable task state persist locally for the documented workflow. The submitted artifact specifies no service, scheduled task, or privileged fact-checking process; sudo appears only in optional package-install examples.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Sending selected claims to Cue, retrieving reports, saving local copies, and optional document conversion fit the disclosed purpose. The [publisher repository](https://github.com/sensedeal/cue-skills) corroborates this workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use a reviewed, fixed runner version with limited local access, and keep sandbox protections enabled. Configure the API key privately rather than pasting it into chat. Submit only content you are comfortable sending to Cue, which processes the request remotely and may consume credits.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Runner installation supports the disclosed API workflow, so the purpose-mismatch claim is unsupported. Automatic updates followed by credential-bearing execution do leave a concrete review and containment concern.
[TP4] expected: The conversion-only mismatch claim overlooks the separate research runner invocation. Pandoc conversion is explicitly documented as an auxiliary feature.
[SC2] expected: The cited pipeline supplies response data to json.load inside fixed Python code; it does not execute downloaded Python. This allegation is unsupported by the cited command.
[PE2] expected: Both occurrences concern ordinary optional installation of Pandoc or LaTeX through the operating-system package manager. They do not establish unauthorized privilege escalation.
[SDI-4] expected: The diagnostic captures the key for authentication without printing it to the conversation. The material ambiguity is the separate instruction to send the key to the agent despite the stated prohibition on viewing it.
